name: Sapphire crystal watch glass

card.summary: A synthetic-sapphire watch cover that resists scratches, keeping a watch face clear and a polished accessory looking new.
card.note: Harder to scratch than glass or acrylic, but costlier and can crack on hard impact.

quick.overview:
A sapphire crystal is the transparent cover over a watch dial made from synthetic sapphire. It is the most scratch-resistant of the common watch crystal materials.

For style, it keeps a watch looking clean and sharp over years of wear, which matters because a watch is a visible part of a person's put-together look.
quick.how: Buyers look for sapphire on the spec sheet when choosing a watch; it appears in mid-range and luxury models, sometimes with an anti-reflective coating. It needs no routine care beyond cleaning.
quick.risks: Sapphire is the most expensive common crystal because it is hard to cut and polish. No health risks; hard impacts can still chip or crack it.

lead: A sapphire crystal watch glass is the clear cover of a wristwatch made from synthetic sapphire. Among common watch crystals (acrylic, mineral glass, sapphire-coated mineral and synthetic sapphire), it is described as the most scratch-resistant.[1]

Its appearance benefit is practical: the dial stays unmarked, so the watch continues to look sharp as part of an outfit. The tradeoff is cost, since sapphire is difficult to cut and polish and so makes the most expensive crystals.[1]
Acrylic, by contrast, is the most impact-resistant and cheapest option, and is used on dive and military watches.[1]

chain: Dial stays clear after daily wear
angle.text: Sapphire protects the dial from scuffs, so a watch continues to look new when worn daily.

paras: Watch crystals come as acrylic (hesalite), tempered mineral glass, sapphire-coated mineral and synthetic sapphire.[1] Sapphire is the premium choice because of its scratch resistance.[1]
Product pages list the crystal material; sapphire is typically marked as such, and some listings note coatings. Acrylic remains common on dive and military watches because it resists impact.[1]
